note: 수동 큐레이션. 공식 발표·공연장 일정(StagePick)·정리 사이트(Songkick, kconcertguide, Soompi, kpopofficial)를 교차 확인해 선별한 목록이며 전수가 아니다. 지난 공연은 자동으로 숨겨진다. intl=true 는 내한공연 섹션에 컴팩트하게 노출.

items.title: PLAVE Concert
items.note: PLAVE are a virtual idol group — the members perform live through motion-captured animated avatars, and the show is built around large-screen staging. One of the few K-pop acts you genuinely cannot experience the same way anywhere else.

items.title: NCT 127 5th Tour — NEO CITY: SEOUL
items.note: Three nights at Korea's main indoor K-pop arena to open the fifth NCT 127 tour. KSPO Dome sits inside Olympic Park on subway lines 5 and 9 — one of the biggest K-pop bookings of the autumn, so expect the presale to decide most seats.

items.title: The Fact Music Awards
items.note: A stadium-scale awards night with a long performance lineup rather than a single headliner. Awards shows are the easiest way to see many groups in one evening, and they are announced months ahead — useful if you are planning a trip around one.

items.title: Silica Gel Asia Tour — Seoul
items.note: Not idol pop — Silica Gel are the biggest name in current Korean indie rock, closing an Asia tour with two arena nights. The pick if your taste runs to bands rather than groups, and tickets are far gentler to get than for idol shows.

items.title: OBJET K-POP FESTA
items.note: A two-day multi-artist festival at the KINTEX convention centre, about 40 minutes from central Seoul on Line 3. Festival line-ups are usually revealed in stages, so check the official channels close to the date.

items.title: &TEAM Tour — BLAZE THE WAY, Seoul Encore
items.note: Encore Seoul dates closing the HYBE Japan group's tour — a crossover act with a strong international fanbase, at the Olympic Park arena over the Chuseok holiday weekend.

items.title: EDC Korea (Electric Daisy Carnival)
items.note: The Korean edition of the Las Vegas mega-rave: two days of EDM stages at the arena-resort complex next to Incheon Airport. Hotels on site and an airport rail link make it one of the easiest festivals in Korea to fly in for.

items.title: AKMU Concert — Paradise of Rumors
items.note: The sibling duo beloved across every Korean generation, playing three arena nights. Less light-stick spectacle, more songwriting and sing-along — a good pick if you want Korean pop beyond the idol format.

items.title: tripleS World Tour — Andless, Seoul
items.note: The 24-member rotating girl group at Jangchung Gymnasium — a compact old-school arena in central Seoul on Line 3, which means closer sightlines than the dome shows.

items.title: Grand Mint Festival
items.note: Seoul's picnic-blanket autumn festival: indie, acoustic and band line-ups across outdoor stages in Olympic Park. The gentlest possible introduction to Korean festival culture — bring a mat, not earplugs.

items.title: ILLIT Concert
items.note: INSPIRE Arena sits next to Incheon Airport, which makes it unusually convenient if you are flying in for the show — the resort complex has hotels on site and an airport rail link into Seoul.

items.title: EXO PLANET #6 — EXhOrizon, Seoul
items.note: Second-generation royalty on a full-group arena run — three nights at KSPO Dome. Expect the fastest sell-out of the season; if general sale fails, plan around the official cancellation-ticket release.

items.title: Melon Music Awards
items.note: One of the year's biggest K-pop nights, held over two days at Korea's only domed stadium. Gocheok is inside Seoul on Line 1, so it is the most accessible of the large-venue events for visitors without a car.

items.title: The Weeknd — Hyundai Card Super Concert
